attempted_claim: Let d in {4,5,6}, a>0, L_a=-Delta+a|x|^{-2}, and (i partial_t - L_a)u = -|u|^{4/(d-2)}u with u(0)=u_0 in H^1(R^d) nonradial. Let E_a(u)=1/2||u||_{dot H^1_a}^2-(d-2)/(2d)||u||_{L^{2^*}}^{2^*} and let W solve -Delta W=|W|^{4/(d-2)}W. Assume E_a(u_0)=E_0(W) and ||u_0||_{dot H^1_a}>||W||_{dot H^1}. For the maximal-lifespan dot H^1_a solution u on (-T_*,T^*), does finite-time blow-up hold in both directions, i.e. T_*<infty and T^*<infty?
decisive_failure: The investigation established virial-sign and nonemptiness facts and diagnosed the target as coinciding with an explicitly open problem, but produced no proof or disproof of the two-sided blow-up claim and no independently valuable emergent result. The blocking obstacle (translation escape shadowing the free W^+ heteroclinic) was analyzed but not overcome.
